title: axe select-name: six filter <select> elements have no accessible name
description: axe-core rule `select-name` (impact: critical), 6 instances across 4 tabs at runtime. Screen-reader users hear only "combo box" with no indication of what each filter does. Locations: MapExplorer.tsx:853 (species filter), :872 (county filter), :896 (media filter); SpeciesDetail.tsx:604 (county filter); LifeList.tsx:616 (county filter, the Multimedia tab); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376 (county filter). The visual label is a decorative MapPin icon with pointerEvents:'none', so nothing names the control. Checklists.tsx:629/:644 does this correctly with aria-label="Protocol"/"County" — that tab had zero select-name violations, proving the in-house fix pattern.
fix: Add aria-label to each select, matching the Checklists.tsx pattern: aria-label="Species filter" / "County" / "Media type" on the MapExplorer selects, and aria-label="County" on the SpeciesDetail, LifeList, and BreedingCodeList county selects.

verdict.reasoning: All six selects verified bare: MapExplorer 853/872/896 (SidebarLabel is an unassociated div), SpeciesDetail 604, LifeList 616, BreedingCodeList 376 (decorative MapPin only); grep confirms no aria-label/title on any of them, while Checklists.tsx 629/644 has the in-house aria-label fix. Accessible name computes to empty, so SR users hear only the current value with no control purpose — axe select-name at critical impact is fairly rated for six primary filter controls across four tabs. Minor imprecision only: for the three MapExplorer selects the visual label is the SidebarLabel div, not a MapPin icon.

title: Filter form controls have no programmatic label across most data tabs
wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (also 2.4.6) AA
description: The county <select> and From/To date inputs are repeated across tabs with no aria-label, no <label for>, and no association to any visible text — a screen-reader user hears an unnamed combobox and two unnamed, indistinguishable date fields. Locations: LifeList.tsx:616 (county select), :644 and :658 (date from/to); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376, :408, :424 (same trio); SpeciesDetail.tsx:604, :629, :643 (same trio). Related instances where a VISIBLE label exists but is not programmatically associated: MapExplorer.tsx:853 (species select), :872 (county select), :896 (media select) and :862/:864 (date text inputs) — their 'Species'/'County'/'Media'/'Date Range' headings are SidebarLabel <div>s (map/MapSidebarUI.tsx:35-43), so the selects have no accessible name and the two free-text date inputs are distinguishable only by the placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD' (format instruction also vanishes once filled — 3.3.2); Settings.tsx:1214, :1226, :1238 (Latitude/Longitude/Radius number inputs whose labels are plain <div>s at :1213/:1225/:1237); ChecklistComparer.tsx:350-353 ('Checklist A/B' <label> elements with no htmlFor, so the inputs' name falls back to the example-URL placeholder). Checklists.tsx:629-663 does this correctly (aria-label="Protocol"/"County"/"From date"/"To date"), proving the house pattern exists.
fix: Match the Checklists.tsx pattern: add aria-label ("County", "From date", "To date") to the bare selects/date inputs in LifeList, BreedingCodeList, SpeciesDetail. In MapExplorer, render SidebarLabel as a <label htmlFor> (or add aria-label to each control), and give the two date inputs distinct names ("Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)"). In Settings, convert the Latitude/Longitude/Radius caption <div>s to <label htmlFor> with input ids. In ChecklistComparer, add htmlFor/id to the existing <label> elements.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every cited location in current code: LifeList/BreedingCodeList/SpeciesDetail county selects and date inputs have no aria-label/label/title; MapExplorer's SidebarLabel is a bare <div> (MapSidebarUI.tsx:35-43) so its selects are unnamed and the two text date inputs share the identical 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder; Settings lat/lon/radius captions are plain <div>s; ChecklistComparer's <label> has no htmlFor and doesn't wrap the input. Checklists.tsx really does carry the aria-label house pattern the fix cites, and ACCESSIBILITY.md discloses only chart-label contrast as a known exception, not this. Serious is the right severity — repeated unnamed form controls across most data tabs is a genuine 4.1.2/1.3.1 SR barrier, though the controls remain operable.
verdict.fixNote: The fix is correct and convention-consistent (mirror Checklists.tsx's aria-label="County"/"From date"/"To date"). One caveat: do not unconditionally convert SidebarLabel to <label htmlFor> — it also captions the Breeding Code SegControl, a button group with no labelable element. Either add aria-label per control in MapExplorer (including format-bearing names like 'Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)' on the free-text date inputs), or give SidebarLabel an optional htmlFor prop that renders <label> only when an id is passed.

title: Selected state not programmatically exposed on segmented controls and toggle pills
description: The shared SegControl renders plain <button>s whose active option is conveyed only by background/border/font-weight — no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radiogroup semantics. It is used for the Map Explorer radius (MapExplorer.tsx:700), breeding filter (:881), Pins/Heatmap display mode (:912), and All/Week (:1285). The same style-only-state defect appears in SpeciesDetail.tsx:1189 (Pins/Heatmap map-mode buttons), BirdingStats.tsx:541 (accumulation granularity), :1628 (breeding filter pills), :1717 (media view mode), ListComparer.tsx:215 (My List / Upload source buttons), and MapExplorer.tsx:1030 (hotspot kind-legend toggles, whose only state cue is opacity 0.4). A screen-reader user cannot tell which option is active. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md: "Filter pills announce whether they are pressed." The codebase already has the correct pattern (SortSeg in Checklists.tsx:74, SnowMap.tsx:144, SpeciesDetail graph groups :962/:974).
fix: Add aria-pressed={value === opt.value} (or role="radio"/aria-checked inside a role="radiogroup") to SegControl's buttons and to each listed location; wrap each group in role="group" with an aria-label.

verdict.reasoning: SegControl (MapSidebarUI.tsx:15-29) renders plain buttons with style-only active state, and every cited usage checks out: MapExplorer 700/881/912/1285, SpeciesDetail ~1189, BirdingStats 541/1628/1717, ListComparer 215, and the hotspot kind-legend toggles at MapExplorer 1030 whose only state cue is opacity 0.4. The correct pattern does exist in SortSeg (Checklists.tsx, role=group + aria-pressed) and SnowMap.tsx:144, and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'filter pills announce whether they are pressed' claim is contradicted rather than disclosed as an exception. Serious is fair: a screen-reader user cannot determine the active option on roughly ten primary filter/view controls.
verdict.fixNote: Give SegControl an ariaLabel prop rendered as role="group" aria-label on its wrapper div plus aria-pressed={value === opt.value} on each button, mirroring SortSeg in Checklists.tsx (the SidebarLabel above it is not programmatically associated, so the group needs its own label). Apply the same aria-pressed to the inline groups in SpeciesDetail, BirdingStats, and ListComparer; for the kind-legend visibility toggles use aria-pressed={!isHidden} so pressed means shown.

title: Media Targets keyboard path is partial and ACCESSIBILITY.md overstates it
description: Media Target chips are DOM <Marker>s with a click-only <div> (no tabindex/role), so the chips themselves are not operable by keyboard. The only keyboard route to a target popup is the 'Nearest Targets' list (MapExplorer.tsx:1292-1338), which is hard-capped at 10 items sorted by distance from the SEARCH CENTER (nearest10 useMemo, MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) — it is not scoped to the map viewport, does not update on pan/zoom, and shows no over-cap hint. Any target beyond the nearest 10 (easy with a 25-50 mi radius) has no keyboard path at all. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 claims "The Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list works the same way" and that "These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom" — that is true for sightings/hotspots (cap 200, BoundsTracker-driven) but false for targets, so the published statement is currently inaccurate.
fix: Render an InViewMarkerList for targets like the other two modes (items = locationGroups filtered by mapBounds via markersInView, cap 200 with the over-cap hint), keeping 'Nearest Targets' as a convenience list; or at minimum correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center, not viewport-scoped.

verdict.reasoning: Verified TargetMarkers.tsx:69-75: chips are click-only divs with no tabindex/role, and MapExplorer.tsx:453-461 confirms nearest10 is distance-from-search-center, slice(0,10), with no mapBounds dependency — so targets beyond the nearest 10 have no keyboard route at all, unlike sightings/hotspots which use markersInView (cap 200, viewport-driven) into InViewMarkerList. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13's claim that the targets list 'works the same way' and is 'scoped to the current map view' is factually wrong for this mode. Genuine 2.1.1 Level A gap in a primary feature plus an inaccurate published statement; serious stands.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested InViewMarkerList fix is correct and matches existing conventions, with two precisions: (1) the locId grouping currently lives in TargetMarkers.tsx's locationGroups useMemo, so either lift it to MapExplorer (shared with displayedTargetPins) or recompute it there before feeding markersInView, and wire onActivate to the existing setSelectedTargetLocId + setPanTarget pair (same owner the chip click uses); (2) per CLAUDE.md, update ACCESSIBILITY.md in the same change — either to truthfully describe the viewport-scoped list once built, or immediately to state that the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center.

title: Inline error messages are silent to assistive tech (no role=alert/aria-live, no aria-describedby)
description:
Several async form-submission error paths render a plain styled
//

, so a screen-reader user who activates the control hears nothing and must hunt the page to discover the failure. Locations: MapExplorer.tsx:105 (place-name search failure), :687 (geolocation error), :1006-1011 (Find Hotspots error), :1227-1232 (Find Recent Sightings error); Settings.tsx:300-309 (malformed/failed CSV upload error in FileRow), :476-485 (API-key save error in KeyRow), :1210 (map-location detect error), :1281-1283 (map defaults save error — additionally the text 'Check your values and try again.' does not identify which of the three fields is invalid); ListComparer.tsx:276-280 (my-list load error). None are associated to their input via aria-describedby either. The codebase has correct reference implementations: App.tsx:668+717-736 (role=alert plus aria-describedby on the input), ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, DropZone.tsx:132, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:184.
fix: Give each error container role="alert" (or aria-live="polite" for non-urgent ones), and where the error relates to a specific input add id + aria-describedby on that input (the App.tsx checklist-input pattern). Make the map-defaults message name the offending field, e.g. "Latitude must be between -90 and 90."

verdict.reasoning: Every cited location verified as a plain styled div/span/p (MapExplorer 105/687/1006/1227, Settings 300-309/476-485/1210/1281-1283 including the field-anonymous 'Check your values' message, ListComparer 276-280); grep shows zero role=alert or aria-live in those files. The cited correct reference implementations all exist (App.tsx role=alert + aria-describedby, ChecklistComparer 372, DropZone 132, WeatherTidePanel 184), so this is inconsistent application of an established house pattern. Serious is fair for 4.1.3/3.3.1: async failures on key flows (location search, CSV upload, API-key save) are completely silent to SR users.

title: Mobile filter sidebar: Escape focus-restore is dead code, trap snapshot goes stale, other close paths drop focus — published a11y claim is false
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (and 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap A integrity)
description: Three defects in the one focus trap the app ships: (1) The Escape handler runs `setSidebarOpen(false); filtersButtonRef.current?.focus()` (lines 200-203), but the Filters button is inside the FAB cluster rendered only when the sidebar is CLOSED (`{!sidebarOpen && (<div className="sr-map-fab-cluster">` at line 1446, ref at 1461). While the sidebar is open the ref is null, so the restore is a no-op; the focused element then gets display:none (`.sr-map-sidebar-hidden`) and the browser dumps focus to <body> — the keyboard user restarts from the top of the document. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 51 explicitly claims 'Escape closes it and returns focus to the button that opened it' — that claim is currently false. (2) The focusable list is snapshotted once at open (lines 192-196: `sidebar.querySelectorAll(...)`, then `first`/`last` captured); the sidebar contains a Filters accordion and async-loaded hotspot/target lists, so after content changes Tab escapes the trap into obscured background content (the page behind is not inert). (3) The mobile 'Close filters' button (line 1414) and the backdrop click (line 1400) close via `setSidebarOpen(false)` with no focus restore — same display:none → body drop.
fix: Keep the FAB cluster mounted while the sidebar is open (hide it with CSS/inert) so the ref survives, or restore focus in an effect that runs after sidebarOpen flips to false. Re-query focusables on each Tab keydown (HelpDocs.tsx:258-273 already does this correctly — reuse that pattern). Route ALL close paths (Escape, Close button, backdrop) through one close() that restores focus.

verdict.reasoning: All three defects verified: (1) the FAB cluster with filtersButtonRef renders only when !sidebarOpen (line 1446, ref 1461), so the Escape handler's focus() at line 202 runs while ref.current is null — dead code — and globals.css confirms .sr-map-sidebar-hidden is display:none on mobile, dropping focus to body; ACCESSIBILITY.md line 51's claim is therefore false. (2) Focusables are snapshotted once (lines 192-196) with [sidebarOpen]-only deps while the sidebar content is dynamic. (3) The Close button (1414) and backdrop (1400) close with no restore. Serious is appropriate: every keyboard close path on mobile strands focus, and the published a11y statement affirms the broken behavior.

title: Filter selects and date inputs have no accessible name on four tabs
description: The county <select> and the From/To <input type="date"> controls have no aria-label, no <label>, and no title — a screen reader announces an unnamed combo box / date field. Same defect repeats: LifeList.tsx:616 (select), :645, :659 (dates); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376 (select), :409, :425 (dates); MapExplorer.tsx:853 (Species select), :872 (County select), :896 (Media select) — the visual SidebarLabel is a styled <div> with no htmlFor association — and MapExplorer.tsx:862/:864 (two date text inputs distinguished only by placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD"). Checklists.tsx:629/:644/:655/:663 does this correctly (aria-label on each), proving the intended pattern exists in-repo.
fix: Add aria-label to each control matching the Checklists tab pattern (aria-label="County", "From date", "To date", "Species", "Media"), or convert SidebarLabel to a <label htmlFor> association in MapExplorer.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited location verified: unnamed selects at SpeciesDetail.tsx:604, LifeList.tsx:616, BreedingCodeList.tsx:376, and MapExplorer.tsx:853/:872/:896 where SidebarLabel (map/MapSidebarUI.tsx:35) is a plain styled <div> with no htmlFor; MapExplorer.tsx:862/:864 are text inputs distinguished only by identical 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholders. Minor nit: HTML-AAM makes the placeholder a fallback accessible name on the two text inputs, but both compute to the same string so the fields remain indistinguishable, and the selects have no name at all. Serious is fair and the aria-label fix matches the existing Checklists.tsx pattern.

title: Map fullscreen overlay: no Escape exit and focus tabs into content obscured behind the overlay
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (also 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum, WCAG 2.2 AA)
description: Fullscreen turns the Map Explorer tabpanel into `position: fixed; inset: 0; zIndex: 1200` (App.tsx:1031-1034) with body scroll locked (App.tsx:390-395), but no keydown handler exits it (grep confirms no Escape handler in App.tsx; the only Escape handlers in the app are the sidebar trap, HelpDocs, the combobox, TabNav, WelcomeScreen). The page chrome (tab bar, footer links, other panels' controls) stays in the DOM and in the tab order BEHIND the overlay, so a keyboard user who tabs past the map's controls watches focus vanish under the map — the focus indicator is rendered but fully obscured. Exit is possible only by finding the Exit-fullscreen FAB again. Escape is the universally expected exit for a viewport-takeover, and the obscured-focus walk is disorienting.
fix: While mapFullscreen: add a document keydown listener that exits on Escape (returning focus to the fullscreen toggle), and apply `inert` to the app shell siblings (or trap Tab within the fullscreen panel) so focus cannot land behind the overlay.

verdict.reasoning: Fullscreen overlay styles (App.tsx:1031-1033) and body scroll lock (:390-395) exist exactly as cited; grep confirms no Escape handler or inert/focus-trap for fullscreen anywhere (MapExplorer.tsx:200's Escape handler is the mobile filters-panel trap only). The footer links/buttons and tab bar stay focusable behind the fixed z-1200 panel, so the obscured-focus walk is real; exit is FAB-only. Fairly flagged under 2.4.11 (WCAG 2.2 AA) with a real keyboard-UX gap; moderate is right since a keyboard exit does exist.
verdict.fixNote:
Put the Escape handling inside MapExplorer rather than App: MapExplorer owns onToggleFullscreen AND the sidebarOpen filters trap (MapExplorer.tsx:187-221), which already listens for Escape on document — an independent App-level listener would close the filters panel and exit fullscreen on the same keypress. Exit fullscreen on Escape only when sidebarOpen is false (innermost layer first), returning focus to the fullscreen FAB. For the obscured-focus half, React 19 (in use, ^19.2.5) supports the boolean inert prop — set inert on the header div, TabNav, footer

, and sibling tabpanels while mapFullscreen && activeTab === 'map-explorer'.

title: Light theme: muted text on tinted surfaces falls just under AA (4.27–4.40:1)
description: --sr-text-muted #71717A passes on white (4.83:1) but not on the tinted surfaces it is commonly paired with in light theme: on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.40:1 (inactive segmented-control labels in MapSidebarUI SegControl, the basemap switcher buttons in globals.css:246, the missing-media badges in the target popup TargetMarkers.tsx:92, numerous chips); on --sr-quote-bg = 4.27:1 (Named Birds comment block); on --sr-accent-bg = 4.31:1 (secondary text inside selected rows, e.g. the location line of a selected Nearest Targets row, MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317). Dark theme passes all three (5.27–5.82:1).
fix: Darken light --sr-text-muted to ~#6B6B74 (≈4.6:1 on #F4F4F5) — a single token change; verify it still reads as 'muted' next to --sr-text.

verdict.reasoning: Independent WCAG math confirms the ratios: #71717A is 4.397:1 on #F4F4F5, 4.268:1 on #EFF1F3, and 4.310:1 on #E8F5EE (dark theme passes 5.27-5.82), and the surface-subtle and accent-bg pairings genuinely co-occur at small text sizes (SegControl inactive labels MapSidebarUI.tsx:13+24, basemap switcher globals.css:234/246, TargetMarkers.tsx:92 badges, selected-row secondary text MapSidebarUI.tsx:96+109 and MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317); these are enabled controls, so the inactive-component exemption does not apply. One cited pairing is wrong: the quote-bg comment blocks (NamedBirdRow.tsx:110, Checklists.tsx:350-351) use full-contrast --sr-text, not muted, so that instance never occurs — but the finding stands on the other two surfaces. The proposed #6B6B74 verifies as passing everywhere (4.66-4.80 on the tinted surfaces, 5.28 on white), and changing only the :root value is convention-clean since the token already exists in both themes; not covered by ACCESSIBILITY.md's chart-bar-label exception.

title: Map popups cannot be dismissed with the keyboard (no close button, no Escape)
description: Every app-rendered map popup passes closeButton={false}, and MapLibre's Popup has no built-in Escape handling (verified: no keydown/Escape in maplibre-gl/src/ui/popup.ts), so the only dismissal is a pointer click on empty map. The Map Explorer in-view list rows open popups by keyboard (good) but never close them: onActivate always sets the locId (MapExplorer.tsx:504-512) — re-activating a row with aria-pressed="true" does not toggle it off, so the pressed state is also a one-way lie. Affected popups: SightingMarkers.tsx:111, HotspotMarkers.tsx:141, TargetMarkers.tsx:79, SightingsMap.tsx:61, BirdingStats.tsx:875. A stuck-open popup overlays the map and inserts extra tab stops (eBird links inside it). The AtlasLayer popup (AtlasLayer.tsx:205) is the one that keeps the default close button — proving the styled close button is available.
fix: Either re-enable closeButton (MapLibre renders a real <button aria-label="Close popup">, already themed via .maplibregl-popup-content CSS), or add an Escape keydown handler that clears the selection state, and make in-view list rows toggle (activating the already-selected row calls onSelect(null)). Any one of these resolves it; the row toggle also fixes the aria-pressed semantics.

verdict.reasoning: All five cited popups pass closeButton={false} at the exact lines, maplibre-gl's bundle contains zero Escape handling, and MapExplorer's only Escape handler is the mobile-sidebar focus trap — so popups opened via the keyboard-accessible in-view lists (which one-way set locId, never toggling aria-pressed rows off) have no keyboard dismissal at all. The HotspotMarkers popup adds real eBird-link tab stops, making this user-impacting under WCAG 2.1.1. ACCESSIBILITY.md describes the keyboard open path but does not disclose the missing dismissal; the suggested fix is accurate and convention-aligned (AtlasLayer.tsx:205 keeps the default close button, a real <button aria-label="Close popup"> already themed via .maplibregl-popup-close-button with var(--sr-text-muted) in globals.css:576).

title: Missing-media type icons in Media Targets popup and marker chips have no text alternative anywhere
description: The whole point of a media target is which media types (photo/audio/video) the user is missing, but that information is conveyed exclusively by unnamed inline SVGs: in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97, bare <svg> per missing type, no aria-hidden, no label), in the on-map chip labels (TargetMarkers.tsx:62, MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML), and the keyboard-accessible "Nearest Targets" sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:~1315-1318) show only name/location/distance — they omit missing types entirely. A screen-reader user can find a target but never learn which media it is missing. This also weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that icon-only information "carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader."
fix: In the popup, give each type span role="img" aria-label={`Missing ${t.toLowerCase()}`} (or append sr-only text) and aria-hidden the SVGs; add the missing types as text (visible or sr-only) to the Nearest Targets sidebar rows so the keyboard/SR path carries the full information.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all three cited surfaces: popup spans (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97) hold bare unnamed SVGs with no role/aria-label/sr-only text, chip labels inject raw MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (line 62, mapExplorerFormat.ts:30-34) with no ARIA, and the Nearest Targets sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:1315-1319) render only name/location/distance — missingTypes never appears as text on any keyboard/SR path. The type-filter pills filter the set but don't convey per-target info, so the feature's core information is icon-only, contradicting ACCESSIBILITY.md line 19's hidden-label claim. Moderate is the right severity: SR users can reach targets but lose the missing-media detail.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested fix is right; extend it slightly: also add aria-hidden="true" into the three MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts so browse-mode screen readers don't hit unnamed images on the on-map chips, and for the sidebar rows reuse the existing sr-only span pattern already used for the recency dot at MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313 (e.g. Missing photo, audio).

title: Map Explorer mobile filter focus trap snapshots focusables once — focus can escape as content changes
description: The mobile filter sidebar trap queries focusable elements once when the overlay opens and captures first/last in the closure (lines 192-196). The sidebar's content is highly dynamic — the Filters accordion expands, the hotspot legend and in-view marker lists appear after a fetch and update on every pan/zoom, Show-all reveals rows. Once elements exist after the stale `last`, Tab from the actual last element is not intercepted and focus walks out of the modal into the backdrop-covered page; elements past the stale `last` are also skipped by the wrap. Escape + focus return (lines 200-203) work correctly. HelpDocs already implements the correct pattern (re-query inside the keydown handler, HelpDocs.tsx:261-263).
fix: Move the querySelectorAll inside handleKeyDown so first/last reflect the live DOM on every Tab press, matching HelpDocs.tsx.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: lines 192-196 snapshot focusables once with effect deps [sidebarOpen], while the sidebar holds the collapsible Filters accordion, async hotspot/target lists, and viewport-scoped in-view marker lists that change on every pan/zoom — so the captured last goes stale and Tab from the real last element walks out of the non-inert overlay. HelpDocs.tsx 255-275 re-queries inside the keydown handler exactly as the fix says, so the fix matches house convention. One factual error in the description — 'Escape + focus return work correctly' is wrong (the restore is dead code, see finding 4) — but it doesn't affect this finding's core claim; moderate is right (it partially duplicates finding 4's defect #2, and 2.4.3 is arguably the better SC tag than 2.1.2).

title: 'Nearest Targets' list is not scoped to the map view and does not update on pan/zoom, contrary to the statement
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md says the Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list 'works the same way' as the in-view lists and then asserts 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom (very dense views are capped, with a "zoom in to narrow the list" hint).' The keyboard path itself is real (each row has a focusable, aria-labelled locate button at lines 1320-1333 that opens the same popup and pans). But `nearest10` (lines 453-461) is computed as the 10 closest pins to the SEARCH CENTER lat/lng inputs — it ignores `mapBounds`, never reacts to panning or zooming, and has no over-cap hint. Only the 'Sightings in view' and 'Hotspots in view' lists (markersInView + mapBounds, cap 200, MapSidebarUI.tsx:118-121) match the published description. A screen-reader user following the statement would expect the targets keyboard list to track the viewport; it doesn't.
fix: Either scope the targets list with markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) like the other two lists, or correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the 10 nearest to the search center.

verdict.reasoning: nearest10 (MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) is sorted by distance from the lat/lng search-center inputs with deps [displayedTargetPins, lat, lng] — it never reads mapBounds, never reacts to pan/zoom, and has no over-cap hint — while ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 explicitly includes the Nearest Targets list in 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom'. The gap is functional, not just a claims bug: target chips are DOM divs with onClick but no tabIndex (TargetMarkers.tsx), so targets beyond the 10 nearest to the center have no keyboard path at all while mouse users can click any chip. Moderate is fair (false published assistive-behavior claim plus a real 2.1.1 gap).
verdict.fixNote: If scoping to the viewport, reuse the existing pattern rather than patching nearest10: derive markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) and render through the shared InViewMarkerList (MapSidebarUI.tsx) like sightingsInView/hotspotsInView, which gives the cap + 'zoom in to narrow the list' hint for free. Otherwise the one-line ACCESSIBILITY.md correction ('the targets list shows the 10 nearest the search center') is the cheaper honest fix.

title: Placeholder-only (or format-only) accessible names on text inputs; Map Explorer From/To dates are indistinguishable
wcag: 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA / 1.3.1 Info and Relationships A
description: Several inputs have no label or aria-label, so the accessible name falls back to the placeholder. Worst case: the Map Explorer date-range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862,864) both have placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD" — a SR user hears the format string twice with nothing distinguishing From vs To (the visible "Date Range" SidebarLabel is not programmatically associated). Same pattern: MapExplorer.tsx:84 (place search), 689/691 (Latitude/Longitude), 1182 (target species search); Settings.tsx:1216/1228/1240 map-default inputs, whose visible "Latitude"/"Longitude"/"Radius (mi)" labels are unassociated <div>s so the computed name is "e.g. 37.8275"; SpeciesDetail.tsx:1268 and MediaCommentsSection.tsx:70 comment filters (placeholder is at least descriptive there, but disappears once text is typed for sighted users). Contrast: Checklists.tsx:655/663 date inputs do it right with aria-label="From date"/"To date".
fix: Add aria-label to each (e.g. "From date (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "To date (YYYY-MM-DD)", "Latitude", "Longitude", "Search by place name"), or associate the existing visible labels via htmlFor/id.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every cited input: MapExplorer 862/864 are both placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" with the 'Date Range' SidebarLabel an unassociated div, so From and To compute identical accessible names; 84, 689/691, 1182, Settings 1216/1228/1240 (visible Latitude/Longitude/Radius labels are plain divs), SpeciesDetail 1268, and MediaCommentsSection 70 all have placeholder-only names. Checklists.tsx 655/663 confirmed as the in-house aria-label="From date"/"To date" pattern the fix mirrors. Moderate is right — placeholders provide a partial name fallback, but the indistinguishable date pair is a genuine 2.4.6/1.3.1 failure.

title: Map sidebar filter inputs rely on placeholders for their accessible names; date inputs are named 'YYYY-MM-DD'
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions A)
description: The Map Explorer sidebar inputs have no <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby — the SidebarLabel headings are unassociated styled divs. Accessible names therefore fall back to placeholders: the two Date Range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862-865) both compute to the meaningless, identical name "YYYY-MM-DD" (a screen-reader user cannot tell From from To, or that they are date filters at all); Latitude/Longitude (:689-692), "Search by place name" (:86), and "Search species…" (:1182) are intelligible but vanish once a value is typed. The adjacent Search button (:90-103) has only a title attribute for its name.
fix: Add aria-label="Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)" (and aria-labels echoing the other placeholders), or give SidebarLabel an id and reference it via aria-labelledby plus a per-field qualifier. Give the search icon button aria-label="Search". (Flagging here because these gate the map experience; may overlap with a forms-dimension audit.)

verdict.reasoning: Verified at MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 the two date inputs are type=text with identical YYYY-MM-DD placeholders and no label/aria-label/aria-labelledby, and SidebarLabel (MapSidebarUI.tsx) is an unassociated styled div; lat/lng (:689-692), place search (:84), species search (:1182) are placeholder-named and the search button (:93) is title-only. One nuance: per HTML-AAM a placeholder remains the computed accessible name even after a value is typed (the 'vanish' is visual-only, a 3.3.2 issue), but the identical meaningless names on the two date fields are a genuine 4.1.2/3.3.2 failure that gates the map filters. Severity moderate is appropriate and the aria-label fix matches existing codebase patterns (e.g. the heatmap slider's aria-label at :930).

title: Map Explorer async error messages are silent to assistive tech
description: The hotspot search error (:1006-1011) and media-targets search error (:1227-1232) render as plain styled divs after an async failure — no role="alert" or aria-live, so a screen-reader user who pressed "Find Hotspots"/"Find Recent Sightings" gets no feedback that the request failed (the role="status" loading chip just disappears). Other error paths in the app do this correctly (ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, App.tsx:720, DropZone.tsx:132).
fix: Add role="alert" to both error divs (matching ChecklistComparer's pattern).

verdict.reasoning: Verified: hotspotsError (1006-1011) and targetsError (1227-1232) render as plain divs with an aria-less AlertCircle icon, no role/aria-live anywhere in MapExplorer per grep, and the role=status loading chip (1437) simply unmounts on failure — so an SR user gets no failure feedback. Cited reference implementations (ChecklistComparer 372, App 720, DropZone 132) all exist, and role=alert on these two divs is the correct house-pattern fix. Note this is a strict subset of finding 11 (same two MapExplorer locations); confirmed independently at moderate, but the two should be deduplicated when applying fixes.

title: Placeholder is the only label on search/filter, coordinate, and API-key text inputs
description: These text inputs have no label or aria-label; their only identification is the placeholder, which disappears as soon as the user types (and browsers' placeholder→accessible-name fallback is a last resort, not a reliable label). Locations: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-70 ('Filter media comments…'); Checklists.tsx:161-165 (shared CommentSearchBox, placeholders 'Filter checklist comments…' / 'Filter species comments…' at :544/:555); SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1268 ('Filter comments…'); MapExplorer.tsx:82-84 ('Search by place name'), :689/:691 (Latitude/Longitude number inputs — after entry a sighted user sees two bare numbers with nothing saying which is which), :1182-1184 ('Search species…'); Settings.tsx:424-428 (API key entry, 'Paste your API key' — the row label at :352 is an unassociated <div>). Impact is worst for low-vision and cognitive users mid-entry, and for the lat/lng pair where the only differentiator vanishes.
fix: Add aria-label to each input (e.g. aria-label="Filter media comments", aria-label="Latitude", aria-label="eBird API key") while keeping the placeholder as a hint; for the Map Explorer lat/lng pair, prefer small visible labels like the Settings map-defaults section already has.

verdict.reasoning: Read every cited input: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-79, the shared CommentSearchBox in Checklists.tsx:161-175 (both instantiations), SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1277, MapExplorer.tsx:82-89/:689-692/:1182-1185, and Settings.tsx:424-440 — none has an aria-label, aria-labelledby, or associated <label>; the placeholder is the only identification, and the Settings row label is an unassociated <div>. ACCESSIBILITY.md's only disclosed exception is chart-bar contrast, so this is undisclosed. Moderate is correct: placeholder fallback usually yields *some* accessible name, but it vanishes on input (worst for the bare lat/lng number pair, which affects sighted users too) — a fair 3.3.2 AA failure, not serious, not pedantry.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested aria-labels are right and match the file-local convention (Checklists.tsx already puts aria-label on its Protocol/County selects and From/To date inputs; MapExplorer/Settings use aria-label heavily elsewhere). One refinement: CommentSearchBox is a shared component, so add a single aria-label derived from its existing title/placeholder prop (e.g. aria-label={placeholder.replace(/…$/, '')}) — one change covers both Checklists instances. For Settings, derive it from the row's label prop (aria-label={`${label} API key value`} or similar) rather than a hardcoded string, since the component renders multiple key rows.

title: External links open new windows without any indication (inconsistent across the app)
description: 43 target="_blank" anchors exist across ~20 component files; only two indicate the behavior — App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 use "(opens in new tab)" in aria-label. All others give no warning, including every link in the Help documentation (HelpDocs.tsx:61 renders all HELP.md links with target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" and no indication), the footer GitHub link (App.tsx:1101-1110), SpeciesLinks.tsx:20/45 (whose aria-labels "View X on eBird" omit it), LifeListTable.tsx media-count links, BirdingStats.tsx checklist/region links (15 instances), Checklists.tsx, MapExplorer.tsx, SpeciesDetail.tsx, NamedBirdRow.tsx, Settings.tsx, WeatherTidePanel.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx, MediaStatsSections.tsx, ChecklistComparer.tsx, SightingsMap.tsx, map/HotspotMarkers.tsx, map/TargetMarkers.tsx, AtlasLayer.tsx, speciesDetail/ui.tsx, CommentText.tsx. Unexpected context changes disorient screen-reader and cognitive-disability users; the app already has the right pattern in two places — it just isn't applied consistently.
evidence: HelpDocs.tsx:61 `<a key={ki++} href={lm[2]} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` with no new-window indication; grep shows 43 target="_blank" instances, only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 carry "(opens in new tab)".
suggestedFix: Adopt one shared ExternalA component (or extend SpeciesLinks' pattern) that appends "(opens in new tab)" to the accessible name (visually-hidden span or aria-label suffix) and use it for all target="_blank" anchors, including HelpDocs' renderInline link branch.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by grep: exactly 43 target="_blank" anchors across 20 component files, with only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 announcing '(opens in new tab)'; HelpDocs.tsx renders every documentation link target="_blank" with no indication and SpeciesLinks.tsx aria-labels omit it. This is the new-window-indication aspect, explicitly distinct from confirmed #53 (which covers the ↗ links' accessible names), so not a duplicate. Correctly scoped as advisory (G201; 3.2.5 is AAA), so minor severity is right; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: A shared external-link component is sound; prefer a visually-hidden span suffix over aria-label so existing link text is preserved, and where an aria-label already exists (SpeciesLinks, icon-only links) append to the label, matching the wording already used at App.tsx:748/898. For icon-only favicon links keep title in sync with the label.

title: Mobile filter-panel focus trap snapshots focusables once at open — focus can escape after content inside the panel changes
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (published claim: 'keeps it there while open')
description: The statement says opening the Map Explorer filter panel 'moves focus into the panel and keeps it there while open' — and the trap (MapExplorer.tsx:187-221) does focus the first element, wrap Tab/Shift+Tab, and return focus on Escape. However `focusable` is queried once when the panel opens; the wrap comparison uses the stale `first`/`last` references. The panel's content is dynamic (the Filters accordion expands, async hotspot/target fetches append in-view list rows after the snapshot's last element), so after such a change, Tab from the true last element no longer matches `last` and focus walks out of the overlay onto the map content behind the backdrop. Edge case, but it makes the 'keeps it there' claim conditionally false.
fix: Re-query the focusable list inside the keydown handler (or on each Tab press) instead of capturing first/last at open time.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: the trap (lines 187-221, deps [sidebarOpen]) snapshots focusables once and wraps against captured first/last, while the sidebar's content is dynamic — the in-view marker lists and the async 'Find hotspots'/targets search results all render inside sidebarRef, so Tab from a newly-appended true-last element escapes the overlay, contradicting the ACCESSIBILITY.md 'keeps it there while open' claim. One correction: the Filters accordion expansion does NOT change the focusable set (its collapsed content stays in the DOM, merely clipped by maxHeight:0, and is already in the snapshot); the async list mutations are the real escape path. Edge case on mobile only, so minor is right; ACCESSIBILITY.md states the opposite, which is a claim, not a disclosure.
verdict.fixNote: Re-query `sidebar.querySelectorAll(...)` inside handleKeyDown on each Tab press and derive first/last from the live list. While there, filter to visible elements (e.g. `el.offsetParent !== null`) so the controls clipped inside the collapsed Filters accordion (maxHeight:0, overflow:hidden — still tabbable today) stop being invisible tab stops.

title: Four inline `animation: 'spin …'` styles in MapExplorer bypass the .spin class convention
wcag: 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (policy per ACCESSIBILITY.md) — regression-risk only, no current failure
description: MapExplorer.tsx applies the spinner keyframes via inline style objects instead of the shared `.spin` class at four sites: line 657 (map loading chip, 'spin 1s linear infinite'), line 682 ('Locating…' spinner, 'spin 0.7s linear infinite'), line 1003 and line 1224 (hotspots / media-targets 'Finding…' spinners, 'spin 1s linear infinite'). There is NO current user impact: the reduced-motion kill in globals.css:588-594 uses a universal `*` selector with `!important` longhands, and author !important declarations override inline styles, so these spinners are correctly frozen for reduced-motion users today. The risk is silent regression: these are the only animations in the codebase that escape the `.spin` class, so any future refactor that scopes the RM block to classes (e.g. `.spin { animation: none }`) instead of `*` would leave these four spinning for reduced-motion users with nothing failing visibly. Reported once; all four locations listed here.
fix: Replace the inline `animation:` declarations with `className="spin"` at MapExplorer.tsx lines 657, 682, 1003, and 1224 (matching every other spinner in the app), so all spinner motion flows through the one class the reduced-motion CSS is built around.

verdict.reasoning: All four inline animation:'spin' sites exist as cited and a repo-wide grep confirms they are the only spinners bypassing the .spin class (line 1438 of the same file uses it). The reduced-motion block (globals.css:588-594) is `*` + !important longhands, which does override inline styles, so the finding's no-current-failure, regression-risk-only framing is accurate and fairly flagged against the published reduced-motion commitment in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: Suggested fix is correct and convention-aligned. One caveat: .spin runs at 0.7s while lines 657/1003/1224 use 1s, so adopting the class slightly speeds those three spinners — cosmetic and consistent with the rest of the app; line 682 already matches 0.7s.

title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: several form controls are under the 24px minimum target size
description: Forward-looking 2.2 delta only. The atlas overlay role="switch" buttons are 38x22px (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under the 24px minimum), and several zero-padding text buttons are ~16-18px tall: the API-key Show/Hide button (Settings.tsx:363-373, padding 0, 0.75rem text), the 'Clear filter' underline buttons (LifeList.tsx:694-703, Checklists.tsx:685-690, SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667), and the 'Go to Settings →' banner buttons (App.tsx:611-619, padding 0). Most currently escape 2.5.8 via the spacing exception (no adjacent target within 24px), but that is fragile under layout changes and the small targets are already hard for motor-impaired users under 2.1 best practice.
fix: Bump the switch buttons to at least 24px tall (e.g. 44x24 track) and give the zero-padding text buttons enough padding (or min-height: 24px with negative-margin compensation) to reach a 24x24 hit area.

verdict.reasoning: All cited controls verified: the three hand-rolled role=switch buttons are 38x22 (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under 24), and the padding-0 text buttons exist as described in Settings.tsx:363-373 (Show/Hide), LifeList.tsx:694-703 / Checklists.tsx:685-690 / SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667 (Clear filter), and App.tsx:611-619 (Go to Settings), all at 0.75rem with no padding (~17px hit height). The finding honestly frames itself as a forward-looking WCAG 2.2 delta and acknowledges the spacing exception currently covers most of them, so minor is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The codebase already has a shared ui/ToggleSwitch.tsx (a 30px-tall role=switch button with the label inside) — prefer migrating the three inline atlas switches to it, or if the label-left/switch-right layout must stay, bump the bare track to >=24px tall (e.g. 44x24). For the zero-padding text buttons, padding (or min-height 24 with negative-margin compensation) as originally suggested is fine.

title: Map Explorer Filters accordion button lacks aria-expanded
description: The collapsible filter panel toggle in the sightings sidebar (button at :836, panel collapsed via max-height 0) exposes no expanded/collapsed state — the only cue is the rotated chevron. Every other disclosure in the app does carry aria-expanded (NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76/:440, TabNav.tsx:234).
fix: Add aria-expanded={filterOpen} (and optionally aria-controls) to the Filters button.

verdict.reasoning: The Filters disclosure button (MapExplorer.tsx:835-847) carries no aria-expanded; the only state cue is the rotated ChevronDown, and the panel collapses via maxHeight 0. Verified the cited convention claim: NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76 and :440, and TabNav.tsx:234 all set aria-expanded on their disclosures, so this is an isolated omission. Minor is right and the suggested one-attribute fix (aria-expanded={filterOpen}, optionally aria-controls) is correct and conventional.

title: Map Explorer filters accordion clamps to maxHeight 600px with overflow:hidden — fails closed if content ever exceeds it
description: The collapsible filter panel animates via `maxHeight: filterOpen ? 600 : 0` with `overflow: 'hidden'`. Measuring the current contents (species select, date range, county, breeding seg-control, media select ≈300px at 100%; ≈450-500px at 200% with seg-control wrapping), there is headroom today, so this is not a present-day failure. But the construction fails silently: any future filter addition, or further text growth, pushes the bottom controls (the Media select) past 600px where they are clipped and unreachable with no scrollbar — the classic animated-max-height trap. Flagged so it isn't extended blindly.
fix: Animate with `grid-template-rows: 0fr/1fr` + `min-height: 0` (no hard cap), or raise the open clamp to a generous `maxHeight: 'none'` after the transition ends, keeping 600px only as the transition target.

verdict.reasoning: Line 848 is exactly `maxHeight: filterOpen ? 600 : 0` with overflow:hidden and no scrollbar path; clipped content would be unreachable since the clamped div sits inside the sidebar scroll container. I re-measured at 200% text scale: selects/inputs/SegControl are fixed-height px and only rem labels grow, so contents land ~420-500px — under the clamp, confirming no present-day 1.4.4 failure exactly as the finding states. Fairly-flagged fail-closed construction on a panel that conditionally gains filters (County, Media), kept at minor as forward-looking only.
verdict.fixNote: Both suggested options work; the grid-template-rows 0fr/1fr technique requires `min-height: 0` plus `overflow: hidden` on the inner row and is supported in WKWebView (Safari 16+) and WebView2, so it is safe for the desktop targets. The transitionend→maxHeight:'none' variant is the smaller diff for this inline-styled component.

title: Date-range filter is a native date picker on four tabs but free-text 'YYYY-MM-DD' fields on Map Explorer
wcag: 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA) — advisory; primarily a consistency/usability gap
description: The identical 'filter sightings by date range' function is presented and identified two different ways. Life List (LifeList.tsx:644-669), Breeding Codes (BreedingCodeList.tsx:408-419), Species Detail (SpeciesDetail.tsx:629-654), and Checklists (Checklists.tsx:653-667) all use paired <input type="date"> controls — native picker UI, a Calendar icon, an accent-fill active state, and a '→' separator. Map Explorer alone implements the same function as two <input type="text"> fields whose only identification is the placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD' (MapExplorer.tsx:862-865), under a 'Date Range' sidebar label. A user who has learned the app-wide date-picker idiom reaches the map and must instead hand-type ISO dates with no picker, no format validation affordance, and no visible from/to distinction (the indistinguishable naming is already reported; this finding is the cross-tab inconsistency of widget and identification). The interaction divergence is not a strict 3.2.4 failure (3.2.4 governs identification, and the labels that do exist don't conflict), so this is recorded as an advisory consistency defect with real cognitive-accessibility cost.
evidence: MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 `<input type="text" placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" value={dateFrom} …/><input type="text" placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" value={dateTo} …/>` vs LifeList.tsx:644-647 `<input type="date" value={dateRange.from} …/>` (same pattern on BreedingCodeList.tsx:408, SpeciesDetail.tsx:629, Checklists.tsx:653).
suggestedFix: Switch the Map Explorer sidebar date fields to the same paired <input type="date"> pattern used everywhere else (with the From/To accessible names the prior audit already calls for); keep the visible 'Date Range' SidebarLabel, which the other tabs could in fact adopt.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 uses two <input type="text"> with only a 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder under one 'Date Range' label, while LifeList.tsx:644, BreedingCodeList.tsx:408, SpeciesDetail.tsx:629, and Checklists.tsx:653 all use paired <input type="date"> (one evidence overstatement: Checklists' pair has no Calendar icon or accent-fill active state — those three trimmings are on the other three tabs only, but the core text-vs-native-picker divergence holds). The advisory framing is fair — same function, different widget and identification, with real cognitive/motor cost from hand-typing ISO dates. Distinct aspect and fix from confirmed #56/#59, which cover the accessible-name/placeholder problem on the same inputs.
verdict.fixNote: Switching to type="date" also moots the 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder-as-name issue from #56/#59 — apply the From/To aria-labels (as Checklists.tsx:655/663 already does) in the same change.

title: WCAG 2.2: 12px icon-only eBird link in Nearest Unvisited Hotspots rows is below Target Size minimum
description: The external eBird link in each 'Nearest Unvisited Hotspots' row is an inline-flex anchor whose only content is a 12px ExternalLink icon with no padding, giving a ~12-14px hit target packed between the location-name button and the distance text — below the 24x24 CSS px minimum of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 and a genuinely hard touch/low-motor target. (For comparison, the equivalent crosshair locate buttons at :1326-1330 are 26x26 and pass.)
fix: Give the anchor a fixed 24x24 (or 26x26 to match the crosshair buttons) box with centered icon, e.g. width/height 24 + justifyContent center.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at MapExplorer.tsx:1108-1118: the anchor is inline-flex with no padding around an ExternalLink size={12} icon, giving a ~12px hit target sitting 6px from the flex:1 location-name button on one side and the distance text on the other — under 2.5.8's 24px minimum, and the 6px gap means the spacing exception does not rescue it (the 24px circles of the anchor and the adjacent ~15px-tall name button intersect). The 26x26 crosshair comparison at :1326-1330 checks out. Fairly flagged as a forward-looking 2.2 item; minor is right and the suggested fixed 24x24/26x26 centered box matches the existing crosshair-button pattern.

title: Recency tier is color-alone at a glance (sighted users); the faint 'old' dot compounds it in light theme (1.64:1)
description: The fresh/mid/old recency tiers on the Nearest Targets sidebar dots and the on-map chip backgrounds are differentiated only by color for sighted users; the sr-only labels (MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313) cover screen readers — so ACCESSIBILITY.md's specific claim about hidden labels on recency dots is TRUE — and the popup shows the tier as text ('≤7 days') plus the date, so the information is reachable by interaction. But a color-blind user scanning the list/map cannot rank targets without clicking each one, and the light-theme 'old' dot (#A8D4BB) is also only 1.64:1 against the sidebar surface (its compensating border is --sr-border at 1.27:1).
fix: Show the visible date (already computed) or a tier letter/shape next to each sidebar dot, and give the 'old' dot a ≥3:1 border (e.g. --sr-accent-strong).

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran the WCAG math: light-theme --sr-map-target-old #A8D4BB vs the sidebar's var(--sr-surface) #FFFFFF is 1.64:1 and the dot's --sr-border #E4E4E7 border is 1.27:1 — the reported ratios are exact (the 'old' tier takes the var(--sr-border) border branch at :1310 since its text token isn't 'white'). The sidebar row (:1310-1319) shows name/location/distance but no date or tier text, and the on-map chips (TargetMarkers.tsx) are colored by tier only, so the tier IS color-alone at a glance for sighted users; the sr-only labels (:1311-1313) and the popup's '≤7 days' text + date exist as the finding accurately concedes. Minor is fair given the interaction path, and the fix is valid: --sr-accent-strong exists in both themes (globals.css:30/:131) and is 7.98:1 against the light surface.

title: Inline `outline: 'none'` on ~20 inputs/selects suppresses the designed focus ring app-wide
description: One repeated pattern: form controls styled with inline `outline: 'none'`, which overrides the global input ring (globals.css:556-563, `outline: 2px solid var(--sr-accent)`). The only surviving indicator is the rule's `border-color: var(--sr-accent) !important` (stylesheet !important still beats inline) plus a 12%-alpha shadow — a 1.5px gray→green border tint instead of the designed 2px ring, easy to miss in dense filter sidebars, and weaker than ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs'. Locations: lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:27 (SELECT_STYLE shared by all Map Explorer selects); MapExplorer.tsx:88,690,692,863,865,1184; LifeList.tsx:627,653,667; BreedingCodeList.tsx:388,419,435; SpeciesDetail.tsx:518,613,638,652,1273; Checklists.tsx:170,265; MediaCommentsSection.tsx:75; Settings.tsx:435,1219,1231,1243. Technically still a visible state change (so not a hard 2.4.7 fail), but a significant app-wide degradation versus the global design.
fix: Remove every inline `outline: 'none'` from inputs/selects — the global stylesheet already suppresses the default ring on non-focus-visible states and supplies the 2px accent ring on focus. The per-element onFocus borderColor handlers (e.g. Settings.tsx:437) become redundant and can stay or go.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all claims: 26 inline outline:'none' occurrences match the listed locations, inline style beats the non-!important outline in globals.css:556-563, and only the !important border-color plus the stylesheet box-shadow survive — the designed 2px ring never renders on these controls. However the surviving indicator (1.5px border flipping gray→accent at 4.52:1 light / 9.22:1 dark vs surface, plus a 4px glow, with explicit onFocus borderColor handlers in Settings) is a perceivable, conventional focus treatment, so 2.4.7 AA is not actually failed — the finding itself concedes this. Real as an app-wide design-consistency issue that also makes ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs' claim inaccurate, but a non-failing degradation grades as minor, not moderate.
